Subject: POC planning: HorizonCare evaluation & ownership RACI

Hi Emily / Jonas —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment for the POC:  

Call summary / goals:
- Evaluate Redwood inference for outpatient triage summaries and clinical note generation.
- Primary success criteria: 1) >= 95% uptime during test windows, 2) median generation latency < 1.2s for 512-token prompts, 3) no PHI exfiltration (logs & storage in customer VPC).

Proposed POC plan & timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize SOW and access (Aaron from procurement + security contacts).
- Week 1: Private deployment in HorizonCare Dev VPC; sample dataset ingest and test runs.
- Week 2: Eval run with 3k real-ish prompts (anonymized), quality review with clinical SME.
- Week 3: Performance tuning, quantization profile, final evaluation & review.

Ownership / RACI asks (please confirm owners):
- Infra / infra access: HorizonCare infra team (please confirm point-of-contact). We need someone to approve VPC peering or provide NAT/bastion details.
- App integration (API calls / auth): HorizonCare app team (owner for embedding calls and auth flow).
- Security / compliance: HorizonCare security lead to review SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM requirements.
- Procurement / contracting: HorizonCare procurement to sign SOW and handle any PO/terms.

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm POC success criteria above or propose edits.
2) Share POC point-of-contacts for Infra, App, Security, and Procurement (name + email + role).
3) Confirm whether you'd like Redwood to run in your VPC (private deployment) or on dedicated Redwood-hosted instance for the trial.

Attached is a draft setup checklist and a first-pass SOW that we can iterate on.

Next steps: if you confirm owners and environment choice today, David (SE) and I can schedule the kickoff for Monday and lock in the test dataset.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this is very helpful. Confirming the success criteria look good to us; a couple small clarifications below:  

- Latency threshold: can we confirm the measurement method (p50 vs p95)? We typically track p95 but are OK adapting to p50 for short prompts.
- For PHI handling: HorizonCare will require that logs and model input storage remain in our VPC and that Redwood confirm no long-term indeterminate retention. Our security team will want a short checklist.

POC owners (please loop these folks):
- Infra: Jonas Berg (jonas.berg@horizoncare.com) — infra lead (VPC, peering, NSG rules).
- App Integration: Priya Singh (priya.singh@horizoncare.com) — mobile/api lead.
- Security: Aaron Patel (aaron.patel@horizoncare.com) — security/compliance (SOC2 reviewer).
- Procurement: Linda Cho (linda.cho@horizoncare.com) — procurement lead.

On environment: we prefer private deployment inside our Dev VPC for the trial to validate networking and KMS access.

Next actions from our side: I’ll introduce Aaron & Linda to this thread and have them share the security questionnaire and PO timeline by Tuesday.

Emily Carter
Director of Product, HorizonCare
emily.carter@horizoncare.com

Emily / team —

Thanks — David (SE) here. Quick notes on infra and a suggested runbook:  

Infra & setup notes (for HorizonCare Dev VPC):
- Network: We'll need either a VPC peering or private endpoint. Peering preferred for performance; please share CIDR and a short maintenance window for routing changes.
- Auth: We support mTLS and token-based auth. For private deployment inside your VPC, we recommend KMS-backed key for encrypting KV cache; if you want HSM integration we can check compatibility (Monica cc’d).
- Size & perf: For the evaluation (3k prompts over one week), a 2-GPU small instance pool should be sufficient. We will instrument continuous batching; expect median latencies under 1s in our profiling but we’ll validate on your dataset.

Proposed runbook & owner RACI (please confirm):
- Redwood SE (David Kim): set up image, test harness, and run initial smoke tests (owner).
- HorizonCare Infra (Jonas): enable peering / provide creds for private endpoint (owner).
- HorizonCare App (Priya): provide sample anonymized prompt set and API integration point for testing (owner).
- HorizonCare Security (Aaron): review SOC2 evidence + KMS/HSM checklist and sign off to proceed (responsible).
- HorizonCare Procurement (Linda): review SOW and sign PO (accountable).

Timeline (adjustable):
- Mar 5 — Kickoff + network handoff.
- Mar 6–8 — Deploy private instance, smoke tests.
- Mar 9–13 — Evaluation runs, quality review.
- Mar 16 — Final review and decision meeting.

I’ve attached a playback checklist and a first SOW draft for legal/procurement to review. Monica (security) — any red flags on the HSM/KMS side?

Thanks —

David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com
